## resolveWord() function

Determines whether a `Word` node is statically a known string, and if so, what that string is — the atom of shell-AST static analysis (e.g. "is this word literally `rm`<!-- -->"). A word is static iff every part is a literal after shell unquoting: a bare `Lit` (backslash escapes processed), a `SglQuoted` (including `$'...'` ANSI-C escapes decoded), or a `DblQuoted` containing only literal parts (and not itself a `$"..."` locale translation) — including concatenations of these (`'r'm` resolves to `"rm"`<!-- -->). A word containing any expansion (`ParamExp`<!-- -->, `CmdSubst`<!-- -->, `ArithmExp`<!-- -->, `ProcSubst`<!-- -->), a triggering unquoted `~` (see `options.context`<!-- -->), an unquoted glob metacharacter/bracket expression/`ExtGlob`<!-- -->, potential brace expansion, a `$"..."` locale translation, or an unrepresentable ANSI-C escape has a nonstatic resolution, never a safety judgment (see [WordResolution](./sh-analysis.wordresolution.md)<!-- -->). Failure to complete an observation is separate: host-copy resource refusal and binding failures propagate explicitly rather than becoming a word-resolution result.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export declare function resolveWord(
  word: Node,
  options?: ResolveWordOptions,
): WordResolution;
```

## Exceptions

TypeError if `word.Type` is neither `"Word"` nor `"TypedNil"` — a programmer-error misuse of the API, not an unknown dynamic word value.

[ShAnalyzeResourceError](./sh-analysis.shanalyzeresourceerror.md) when the host exhausts its stack while copying a brace-observation input. This is not a fixed syntax-depth guarantee. Binding and unrelated host failures preserve their own categories.
